subject: Operational readout: checkout latency spike — exec brief & follow-through
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya@fastretail.com>

Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Checkout latency spike impacting US region

Hi Tessa / Laura —

We saw a sudden latency spike starting ~08:50 PT that caused timeouts for checkout on our mobile and web apps. Error rate for token-generation calls to your API jumped from ~0.8% up to 6.4% for requests between 80–120 tokens. This is affecting a subset of our traffic (US-west).

Key impact:
- Checkout conversion drops ~12% during the window
- Several user sessions retried, increasing downstream load

Can you confirm if this is coming from a model or infra regression? We need an ops-level readout within the next 2 hours and an exec summary for our SVP of Core Commerce.

Attached: quick HAR + timeline.

—Priya
Priya Rao
VP Product Operations, FastRetail
priya@fastretail.com

Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout latency spike — quick findings

Quick technical summary from early triage (08:45–09:05 PT):
- Error-rate increase correlated with increased queue depth on the west-2 dedicated pool handling FastRetail traffic.
- Observed elevated tail latencies for sequence lengths > 96 tokens. Kernel selection shifted to fallback fp16 path on several nodes (see runtimes_metrics_20261115.csv).
- KV cache hit rate dropped from 72% -> 34% due to a sudden burst of long prefix requests.

Initial hypothesis: workload pattern changed (more long-seq requests) + a temporary cache eviction/rehydration issue -> increased GPU kernel fallback and queuing. No sign of model weight corruption.

I attached the raw metrics export. I’ll continue digging into the autoscaling log, but recommend immediate mitigation: route long-seq requests to a maintained variant with robust batching behavior for the next 3 hours.

Laura Bennett
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: runtimes_metrics_20261115.csv

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Mitigation plan (temp routing + cache rewarm)

Action plan proposed (immediate containment):
1) Traffic split: 85% default -> 90% stable-quant variant (lower throughput cost but predictable latencies) for sequence lengths > 96 for the next 3 hours.
2) Force KV cache rewarm for FastRetail prefixes; disable aggressive eviction policy for that tenant for 4 hours.
3) Warm standby nodes: bring two additional nodes in west-2 online (manual add to dedicated pool) to absorb burst.
4) Short-term rate-limit increase on retries to avoid client-side retry storms.

I pushed a mitigation-playbook.md draft to the ops bucket and initiated node spin-up at 12:18 PT. Expect measurable latency improvement in ~12–20 minutes after cache rewarm starts.

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mitigation-playbook.md

From: tessa_morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec brief: operational readout for FastRetail — summary + next steps

Priya / FastRetail leadership —

Thanks again for the quick flag. Below is an executive summary of what we found and the immediate actions we took. Full RCA attached.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 08:50–09:25 PT on Nov 15
- Impact: elevated error rate and tail latency affecting checkout flows (conversion impact estimated ~10–14% during peak)
- Root cause (short): cache-eviction cascade + workload shift toward long-sequence requests causing kernel fallback and queueing on west-2 dedicated pool
- Containment steps taken (Nov 15): traffic split to stable variant, KV cache rewarm, spun up 2 warm nodes, applied retry rate-limits. Measurable latency improved by ~60% within 18 minutes of mitigation start.

Requested exec decisions / asks:
1) Approve a temporary increase in reserved capacity for FastRetail west-2 pool for the next 30 days while we finalize the long-term remediation.
2) Accept an automated routing policy change for long-seq traffic (opt-in) to prevent kernel fallback regressions.
3) Sign-off to share post-incident RCA with FastRetail execs (attached).

We’ve attached RCA-v1.pdf for your review. Can we schedule a 20-minute readout with your SVP at 10:30 PT today? Please reply with availability.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Director, Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RCA-v1.pdf
